subject: Snapshot correlator + stakeholder-ready deck for per-route cost/latency outliers
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Snapshot correlator + stakeholder-ready deck for per-route cost/latency outliers

Hey team —

Quick ask following yesterday's post-mortem with Acme: they saw a ~3x token cost spike on one route over a ~20 minute window and want a compact artifact we can share with their platform team that ties the high cost to the exact sequence state (model variant, prefix length, batch size, and the active routing policy) that produced the tokens.

Current problem: console charts show aggregated per-route spend and p95/p99 latency, but it's non-trivial to export a small reproducible snapshot (trace + minimal request sample + config) that the customer or our SREs can use to reproduce or reason about alignment vs. config.

Request: can we surface a "snapshot correlator" action in the route details page that: 
- snapshots a small sample of the request/response traces (redacted) with token-level cost, KV cache hit/miss summary, model variant + quantization profile, and inferred batch size;
- auto-generates a single-page PDF (or slide) summarizing the findings with a recommended next-step (rollback to variant X / reduce seq_limit / escalate to infra);
- attaches the raw snapshot JSON for internal debugging (see example-snapshot.json attached).

Notes: 
- Minimal privacy: snapshots must scrub PII and customer payloads before export (we can reuse the redaction rules from the audit export).
- UX: a small button "Create snapshot for sharing" in the console should default to internal-only but allow an explicit "include for customer" toggle.
- Priority: Acme is asking for this capability for their renewal conversation next week; not a blocker for system stability but high customer-facing priority.

Karthik / Diego — can you quick-scope effort (approx days) and surface any major blockers (data retention, redaction, potential perf impact of collecting token-level traces for long windows)?

Thanks,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot correlator + stakeholder-ready deck for per-route cost/latency outliers

Kim —

Thanks for the clear ask. First-pass estimates / risks: 

Effort estimate (rough):
- Backend: 3-4 dev days to add an export endpoint that composes token-costs + config metadata + trace pointers and runs redaction.
- Runtime: 2 dev days for sampling hooks + a lightweight snapshotter that reads KV cache metadata and batch size inference; could be feature-flagged.
- Console/UX: 2 dev days for a route action + one-page PDF generator (we can assemble a simple template rather than full slide deck).
- QA/security: 1-2 days to validate redaction logic against privacy rules and create automated tests.

Main blockers / risks:
- Data retention & perf: collecting token-level details for very large windows is expensive; we should limit snapshots to a default window (e.g., last 10k tokens or last 15 minutes) and surface a sampling warning.
- Redaction accuracy: will need a short privacy review; if customers include secrets in the prompt we should default to internal-only export until redaction is vetted.
- Attachments & file formats: PDF ok, but many customers want a compact JSON for debugging; we should provide both.

Diego — can you confirm whether current tracing/kv metadata is accessible from the snapshot pipeline without touching the hot path? If not, we should consider a replicated read path which is more effort.

I'll align with Eng leads and follow up with a rough schedule by EOD.

- Karthik

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot correlator + stakeholder-ready deck for per-route cost/latency outliers

Karthik / Kim —

Confirmed: we can surface the KV/cache metadata and per-token cost summary from the async trace store without impacting the serving hot path. A couple of implementation notes: 
- We'll need a lightweight extraction job that pulls traces by trace-id and stitches token costs back to the request — ~3 days to build and test.
- Default snapshot window should be configurable but default to last 5000 tokens or 10 minutes (whichever triggers earlier) to avoid huge payloads.
- Redaction: we should reuse the audit export redactor but add a special-case for generated tool outputs (tool calls) which sometimes contain customer PII; default to internal-only if confidence low.

I'll prototype the trace extractor and a JSON schema sample attached (example-snapshot.json). Once we have the JSON shape we can mock the PDF template and get product review.

Diego

On Tue, Jun 1, 2026 at 11:03 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kim —
> 
> Thanks for the clear ask. First-pass estimates / risks: ...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@acme.com>, acme-platform-eng@acme.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Snapshot correlator + stakeholder-ready deck for per-route cost/latency outliers

Sara — looping you in on our proposed plan. Summary for Acme: we will add a console "Create snapshot" button in the route detail that emits a redacted JSON and a one-page PDF that explains: what model/variant served the traffic, token-level cost highlights, a short latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), KV-cache hit summary, and a recommended next action.

Timeline (tentative): prototype by 2026-06-10, internal QA by 2026-06-15, shareable beta with Acme by 2026-06-21. If this schedule looks tight for your internal review cycle we can prioritize the PDF-only export first and delay raw JSON export.

Action for Acme: can you confirm whether the PDF-only artifact is sufficient for your platform team in the near-term or if they require the raw JSON to attach to a ticket?

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Observability
Redwood Inference
